entries.rule: status table: untested opener at model_first_use_year
entries.note: J Virol 84(1):482, PMID 19812153; both quoted sentences verbatim in abstract. Europe PMC first-publication 2010-01-01; Oct-2009 ahead-of-print not confirmed, year 2010 stands. Abstract already cites clinical proof-of-concept; opener untested still right.

entries.rule: engagement: proximal readout (viral load); evidence rule 1 comparison_stated
entries.note: Nature 465:96, epub 2010-04-21; quote verbatim in abstract, which carries both replicon EC50s and the 3.3 log10 fall, so comparison_stated true holds. Proximal readout, direction only: supported.

Hepatology 54(6):1924, PMID 21809362; quote verbatim (PubMed abstract). Patient-level match supported. Dating: Gao 2010 abstract already states patient variants sat at replicon-identified positions, so this strengthening comparison was public in 2010, not 2011.
Gao 2010 resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Opener untested is right: single-dose PD only, no exposure-versus-EC50 comparison at that date.

entries.rule: dose table row 'reached, drug worked'; rule 7 (no later knowledge) strained, see rule question 1
entries.note: Hepatology 54(6):1956, PMID 21837752; quote verbatim. Target reached (once-daily PK, 2.8-4.1 log10 declines) supported at abstract level; trough/EC50 ratio unread by both of us. 'Drug worked' leans on Lok 2012/ALLY-3 (rule 7); see rule question 1.

entries.rule: dose: same, strengthening; tier 2 regulator document
entries.note: Quote verbatim in bundled ClinPharmR (section 2.2.4.1 and summary; pooled AI447026/AI447028, daclatasvir+asunaprevir GT1b). Flat exposure-response at 60 mg supports a strengthening same; the same passage notes lower SVR with Y93H/L31 variants, as the draft says.
Lemm 2010 resolves (PMID 19812153); quote verbatim in abstract. Opener untested right: resistance sites mapped before any patient dosed.

entries.rule: efficacy: primary endpoint, class-level same; paired comparison (comparison_stated false, model_src Gao 2010)
entries.note: NEJM 366:216, PMID 22256805; quote verbatim; abstract names SVR12 primary. NCT01012895 first posted 2009-11-13, no results, primary 'HCV RNA 12 weeks post-treatment'. Class-level same supported: SVR achieved, 1a breakthroughs with NS5A resistance as the replicon predicted.

entries.rule: decision 10 retrodiction -> retro; 'conditions the model never tested -> untested' for the GT2 pairing, see rule question 2
entries.note: Gut 62:1055, epub 2013-01-15, after Lok 2012; quote verbatim; retro for GT1b supported. But abstract also says combinations 'failed to eradicate' GT2a/2b, and daclatasvir+sofosbuvir cured 92% of GT2 (Sulkowski 2014): draft's 'never tested' is wrong; see rule question 2.

entries.rule: rule 6 dating (earliest source stating the comparison); source_calls_it partial
entries.note: Field year/epub_year/print_year 2015->2014, src -> FDA Harvoni label Oct 2014 (205834s000lbl.pdf, sec 12.4, bundle lines 1105-1127): treatment-experienced baseline NS5A RAP relapse 22% (5/23); quote verbatim. Naive ION-1/3 showed no difference (6% vs 5%), so source_calls_it partial. | superseded: confirmed (): Quote verbatim in bundled label section 12.4; Table 7 (54% 7/13 vs 92% 124/135; cirrhotics 25% 1/4) verified; NCT02032901 results posted 2015-09-14. Patient-level same supported; 2,737-fold figure not re-read. Harvoni Oct-2014 label made the same comparison earlier (missing).
entries.adjudication_note: Status same agreed. Rule 6 dating: Harvoni label Oct 2014 sec 12.4 already pairs baseline NS5A RAPs with relapse (22%, 5/23 treatment-experienced; naive no difference), so year 2014, source_calls_it partial.

entries.rule: efficacy: patient-level same, comparison stated by regulator (tier 2)
entries.note: Quote verbatim in bundled Zepatier label section 12.4; Table 11 (98% 441/450 vs 70% 39/56) verified; NCT02105467 (C-EDGE TN) results posted 2016-04-12, primary SVR12. Patient-level same supported; the positions tested are the replicon's.

entries.rule: status table: untested opener, proxy allowed
entries.note: Nettles 2011 resolves; quote verbatim (abstract). Opener untested with patient-tolerability proxy acceptable. PharmR lists DS07109 (3T3 phototoxicity) but I saw no June-2007 date in the snippet; model_first_use_year 2007 unverified.

entries.rule: safety: model's silence not contradicted -> same; harm from another class set aside (decision 13)
entries.note: Quote verbatim in bundled Harvoni PharmR (safety-pharmacology section, after hERG/dog telemetry); 'No clear target organs ... mice, rats and dogs' also verified. Comparison stated by reviewer; same supported. Later amiodarone bradycardia (2015) is attributed to sofosbuvir, outside class.

entries.rule: safety: predicted harm absent in patients -> contra, magnitude opposite; see rule question 3
entries.note: Quote verbatim in bundled SumR. PharmR margins verified (1-month rat NOAEL AUC 5.07, adrenal hypertrophy >=25.4; 6-month effects >=9.14 ug.h/mL) vs label human 60-mg AUC 10,973 ng.h/mL: ~0.8-2.3x. Contra/opposite by the letter; rule question 3. EMA 2014 dating unverified.

entries.rule: decision 7/8: untested opener at the model's first class use
entries.note: PNAS 110:3991, PMID 23431163, epub 2013-02-19; quote verbatim in abstract. Multiscale model fitted to Gao 2010 daclatasvir kinetics; two-MOA and 45-min half-life predictions tested in vitro only, so untested opener holds. Abstract level.

entries.rule: decision 10: post-hoc model reproducing the known result -> retro
entries.note: J Hepatol 65:1, PMID 26907973, epub 2016-02-22; quote verbatim; abstract states retrospective design, SVR known before fitting; relapser flagged post hoc, so retro patient-level. Member-drug arms are SOF+DCV (19) and SOF+LDV (20); SOF+SMV (19) carries no NS5A drug. Abstract level.

entries.rule: decision 11: pre-specified readout (SVR rate) held with one per-patient miss -> same; member drug in every regimen; see rule questions
entries.note: Sci Rep 10:17820, PMC7575564 full text read. Model fitted to week 0-4 kinetics in real time, TTC binned to 6/8/10/12 wk; regimens SOF/VEL 11, ELB/GRZ 8, SOF/LED 6, GLE/PIB 4, all NS5A-containing. 11 shortened = 10 by model TTC + 1 by day-2 <LLoQ rule (Pt 5, no fit): model-picked cures are 9/10, not 10/11; fix magnitude_basis. Relapser Pt 3 (GT3a, SOF/VEL, TTC 36 d -> 6 wk) relapsed wk 4 post-EOT; paper hedges GT3 might relapse at 12 wk. NCT03603327 first posted 2018-07-27 but started 2018-02-25 (registered after start), no results; year 2020 from epub stands. Same supported; prospective, patient-level.

Field year 2019->2015, src -> Kai 2015 (first author Kai Y, not Kan; J Gastroenterol 50:1145, doi:10.1007/s00535-015-1108-6, PMID 26208695, epub 2015-07-25), model_first_use_year 2015. Abstract confirms TK-NOG mice, LDV/GS-558093 failed. Status untested stands for opener. | superseded: corrected (CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models): Doi 2019 resolves (J Gastroenterol 54:449, published 2019-01-25); quote verbatim; TK-NOG host confirmed from keywords, abbreviation list, ref 19 Hasegawa 2011 and CIEA co-author Suemizu (methods paywalled). Split from the Hiroshima/PhoenixBio cDNA-uPA/SCID track (Osawa 2019 affiliations and refs Tateno 2015, Uchida 2017) is right. But the same Osaka TK-NOG system was first used for the class in Kan 2015 (J Gastroenterol 50:1145, PMID 26208695, epub 2015-07-25: DCV/ASV-failure L31V+Y93H serum into TK-NOG mice, LDV+GS-558093 failed), so the opener is Kan 2015, model_first_use_year 2015, and the model description should drop the per-experiment P32del inoculum. Status untested stands for the opener; Kan's prospective prediction is listed in missing.
entries.adjudication_note: Drafter and checker agree on untested; only the opener date differs. Rule 6 / opener at first class use: Kai 2015 (PMID 26208695) first used TK-NOG for the class, so year 2015. Not the track latest (retro follows); no untested_reason.

entries.rule: decision 10: model run after the patient result was known -> retro, never same
entries.note: Quote verbatim in abstract. Donor serum came from a patient who had already failed LDV/SOF, so the LDV+GS-558093 mouse failure reproduces a known patient result: retro, patient-level, 2019 right. The retro rests on the donor history; Uemura 2019 (epub 2019-01-05, GLE/PIB) is incidental since pibrentasvir was not dosed in the mice. source_calls_it 'match' is the drafter's reading, not stated by the source. Abstract level.

missing: Humanized-mouse track, second prediction: Shi 2013 (doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2012-302600) also reports NS5A+NS3 and NS5A+NS5B combinations 'failed to eradicate the virus in mice infected with HCV genotypes 2a or 2b'; the draft says this was never tested with a member drug, but daclatasvir + sofosbuvir 24 weeks cured 92% (24/26) of genotype 2 patients (Sulkowski 2014, NEJM 370:211, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1306218, NCT01359644; GT2/3 data presented 2012). Conditions differ (4 weeks + non-nucleoside BMS-821095 in mice vs 24 weeks + nucleotide sofosbuvir), so admissibility is rule question 2; either way it belongs on the track.

Earlier regulator patient-level comparison on the replicon track: FDA Harvoni label Oct 2014 section 12.4 (http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2014/205834s000lbl.pdf; bundle sources/205834/205834s000lbl.txt) reports treatment-experienced GT1 subjects with baseline NS5A resistance-associated polymorphisms relapsed 22% (5/23) vs 2% (2/85) after 12 weeks and 0% after 24 weeks. Same status (same, patient-level) nine months before the Daklinza 2015 entry; rule 6 dates the first regulator use of the replicon RAS map to 2014.

Humanized-mouse track, later member-drug retrodictions not in the draft (title/abstract level only, not read in full): 'Efficacy of glecaprevir and pibrentasvir treatment for genotype 1b HCV drug resistance-associated variants in humanized mice' (J Gen Virol 2019, doi:10.1099/jgv.0.001268, PMID 31199224) and 'Combinations of two drugs ... effective for HCV with NS5A-P32 deletion in humanized-liver mice' (J Gastroenterol 2019, doi:10.1007/s00535-018-01541-x, PMID 30684016); both model patient-derived NS5A-failure variants against clinical outcomes.

In-silico track not drawn: the viral-kinetic model fitted to the Gao 2010 daclatasvir patient kinetics (Guedj et al., PNAS 2013, 'Modeling shows that the NS5A inhibitor daclatasvir has two modes of action and yields a shorter estimate of the hepatitis C virus half-life', doi:10.1073/pnas.1203110110) is a model_kind in_silico retrodiction compared with patient data for a member drug. Citation from memory, not re-opened in this check; verify before use.

TK-NOG track, prospective patient-level prediction before the Doi 2019 retrodiction: Kan 2015 (J Gastroenterol 50:1145, doi:10.1007/s00535-015-1108-6, PMID 26208695, epub 2015-07-25; Osaka, TK-NOG) inoculated TK-NOG mice with DCV/ASV-failure serum (NS3 D168V, NS5A L31V+Y93H) and found ledipasvir + GS-558093 failed to achieve EOT or SVR while telaprevir + GS-558093 cured, when LDV/SOF retreatment of DCV/ASV failures was untested in patients. Patient tests followed in 2017 (PMIDs 28315983 J Gastroenterol, 28815329 J Gastroenterol, 28884930 and 28332272 Hepatol Res: LDV/SOF +/- RBV in DCV/ASV failures stratified by NS5A RAS); SVR numbers not read, so same vs contra is open. This moves the TK-NOG opener to 2015 (CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models).

hcv-tk-nog-humanized-liver-mouse 2017 efficacy pairing not yet an entry: Kai 2015 (PMID 26208695) predicted LDV/GS-558093 failure vs DCV/ASV-failure virus (D168V+L31V+Y93H); Suda 2017 (PMID 28315983) SVR 13/15 and Kawakami 2018 (PMID 28815329, epub 2017-08-16) SVR12 26/30 on LDV/SOF+ribavirin 12 wk. Contra is doubtful: patients got ribavirin the mice never got, and Suda credits RBV, so per the untested-conditions rule this likely scores untested.
rule_questions: Dose cell timing: when the model's exposure target is reached and a 14-day monotherapy viral-load decline is near-maximal (Nettles 2011), is that 'reached, drug worked' -> same in 2011, or must dose `same` wait for the SVR primary endpoint (Lok 2012)? The draft's judgement uses Lok 2012 and ALLY-3, which rule 7 forbids; the 2011 source alone supports only PD, not efficacy.

Retrodiction with a split result: one retrodiction paper (Shi 2013) reproduced the known human result in genotype 1b (retro) and predicted failure in genotype 2, where patients were cured under a different duration and NS5B partner (4 weeks + NNI in mice; 24 weeks + sofosbuvir in Sulkowski 2014). Is the GT2 comparison `untested` (conditions the model never tested), `contra` on the mouse track (a retrodiction that failed to reproduce human data, overriding retro by the 'one contra beats same' rule), or a fresh prospective entry under decision 10 if the GT2 human data were not yet public in January 2013?

Safety 'predicted harm': an adaptive, reversible animal finding (adrenal cortical hypertrophy with raised corticosterone in rat and monkey at ~0.8-2.3x the human AUC) that the regulator treated as a monitoring item and cleared on cortisol. Does any target-organ finding near clinical exposure count as a predicted harm (contra, magnitude opposite, as drafted), or only one the model source or sponsor stated as a human risk (the lenient 'same' the draft mentions)? The answer flips the safety track.

Track identity for toxicology: the draft pools every member drug's GLP repeat-dose package into one model_id (ns5a-animal-tox), so daclatasvir's adrenal contra (2015) overrides ledipasvir's same (2014) via 'one drug's contra beats another drug's same on the same track'. Is species-matched repeat-dose toxicology one system across drugs, or does each drug's package form its own track?

Dating by the earliest regulator: the daclatasvir adrenal/cortisol comparison was presumably in the EMA Daklinza EPAR (CHMP opinion mid-2014) before the FDA summary review (July 2015); rule 6 would date the contra to 2014. I could not verify (EPAR PDF download truncated twice); not retried.

In-silico regimen-level models (CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models): the viral-kinetic model estimates whole-regimen effectiveness and would make the same per-patient duration call for any DAA regimen. Does a prospective prediction about an NS5A-containing combination (Etzion 2020: SOF/VEL, ELB/GRZ, SOF/LED, GLE/PIB) count as a class prediction because a member drug is in every regimen, as the tile's trial entries already assume, or must the model's prediction be attributable to the NS5A component (only the Guedj 2013 daclatasvir-monotherapy fit qualifies)?

Track identity for humanized-liver mice (CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models): is host strain the system (TK-NOG, CIEA/Osaka vs cDNA-uPA/SCID, PhoenixBio/Hiroshima: different transgene, injury mechanism and immunodeficiency, same readout), or is 'human hepatocyte chimeric mouse' one platform? If merged, Kan 2015, Doi 2019 and Osawa 2019 join the uPA/SCID track; retro entries never set the headline, so only the 2015/2017 Kan prediction could change a headline.

Per-patient miss inside a prospective patient-level prediction (CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models): Etzion 2020 cured 9 of 10 model-shortened patients and the primary SVR rate held (28/29). Decision 11 covers one readout matched and one not, not 9 of 10 subjects; is this same with source_calls_it: partial and a magnitude bin, or does a patient-level call carry the miss?
could_not_verify: EMA Daklinza EPAR text (download truncated twice; not retried) for an earlier public date of the adrenal and exposure-response comparisons.
Lemm 2010 online-ahead-of-print date (Europe PMC lists 2010-01-01); Fridell and Nettles 2011 online dates (Europe PMC lists print 2011-12-01).
Daklinza label 12.4 replicon fold-shift figures (2,737-fold Y93H, 56-fold A30K, 1.75-fold S62L) and the June-2007 date of study DS07109: not re-grepped.
Tier-1 papers were checked at abstract level only (Europe PMC / PubMed); every quoted sentence sits in the abstract.
Doi 2019 and Kan 2015 methods paragraphs (Springer paywall; host strain taken from keywords, abbreviation list, references and CIEA co-authorship).
SVR numbers of the 2017 Japanese LDV/SOF retreatment studies in DCV/ASV failures (PMIDs 28315983, 28815329, 28884930, 28332272), needed to score the Kan 2015 TK-NOG prediction.
